edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — Point-and-click root — count its cooldown before stepping up. The duo’s tempo bends around it. - Keep E Battle Dance banked for their best play. - The ultimate is a fight decision, not a habit.
edits.after: - Twisted Advance (W) is a point-and-click root, 14s down to 10s at rank 5 — count it before stepping up. - Bramble Smash (Q, 7s down to 5s) grounds: it shuts off your W and E dash outright if he lands it while you're mid-cast. - Ban the ultimate for the swing fight, not a habit.

edits.before: Level 2-3 windows govern; level 6 hardens the playbook; first item funds it.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 you out-poke his sapling chip; level 6's Quickness turns his root engage into a countercharm; first item's mobility exploits his zero-dash kit.

edits.before: Zone with the threat — the button you hold governs more than the one you press.
edits.after: W-Q double-tap out-pokes his sapling chip before level 3 — just track the single point-and-click root, since Bramble Smash grounds any dash you commit mid-cast.

edits.before: Window economy: convert the ganks, start the rivers, peel the picks.
edits.after: His whole kill threat is landing Twisted Advance (W) — dodge that one root and every rootless window from 3 to 6 is yours to punish with a charm all-in.

edits.before: Carry by windows — one clean play per fight; your carry does the arithmetic.
edits.after: Carry by flanking his zero-dash kit — The Quickness catches him stuck walking, and Battle Dance resets onto whichever ally he tries to root instead.

edits.before: You decide the fights your team attends — start them, peel them, or poke them out of existence.
edits.after: Your mobility picks the terms — flank in, charm through Twisted Advance's range, and reset with Battle Dance before his Nature's Grasp wall can seal you in.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: entrance Maokai's carry off every window and charm the recovery formations.
edits.after: Ahead, hunt his root: track Twisted Advance's 14-10s cooldown, flank while it's down, and his kit has no dash to punish the commit.

edits.before: Q the pair for the heal, W the window, E home — the trade paid twice and answered once.
edits.after: Track Bramble Smash's cooldown before you dash — land mid-ground and its 7-5s grounding shuts your W and E off outright.

edits.before: Maokai whiffs Twisted Advance (Root) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: He's untargetable mid-dash on Twisted Advance — spending your burst into that frame wastes it; wait for the root to land or whiff first.

edits.before: That is Maokai’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Bramble Smash grounds — dashing into its 7-5s window shuts your W and E off and strands you in his engage range.

edits.before: Entrancing into a banked disengage — the bird that flies into tornadoes writes the highlight for the other team.
edits.after: Trading extended into his Sap Magic sustain — his auto-heal cooldown keeps refreshing off spell contact, so anti-heal timing decides long fights, not chip damage.
